design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (hosting_plans_and_billing, env_0076), rework round 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,4]; hosting_ext_overdue_renewal took 5 factors, hosting_ext_cloud_upgrade took 4.

WHY A GOOD TEST. The customer asks only for an upgrade (Cloud 4 -> Cloud 8) and says she will pay by PayPal herself. The upgrade rule says 'An upgrade charge is fixed only after the plan's term end date is later than today.' The plan's term ended 2026-10-15 after a fully declined auto-renew cycle (attempts 1-3 on 10-08, 10-12, 10-14) and today is 2026-10-18, so the agent must discover that the overdue renewal is owed, price it (new term from the scheduled 24-month request, reseller discount, domain/mail/certificate bundle credits from three other products' records, per-day late fee), hand it to the customer to pay at checkout, and only then price the upgrade on the renewed term (Cloud 8 term price with no tier discount since the account charter never discounts proration lines, month-based proration, outgrown-plan credit, first-upgrade welcome credit, mail bundle credit) and hand that purchase over too.

OWNER RULING. Both writes are the account holder's own payments at Harborline's checkout (coordinator owner_ruling (b)): the stored card ending 2731 expired and she pays through PayPal, a method not on file; each extended rule states the payment is the holder's own act at checkout after the agent quotes it.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims hosting_ext_overdue_renewal (holder-paid renewal of a plan whose term end date is on or before today, no scheduled downgrade) and hosting_ext_cloud_upgrade (Cloud 4 -> Cloud 8), tools bill_overdue_hosting_renewal_c53aa4e7 and buy_hosting_upgrade_8645a072 (both owner=user). Task 1 holds the auto-renew refund and the early renewal (holder-paid, term end later than today, no scheduled downgrade or term change). Auto-renew charges and downgrade-applying renewals stay under base (both renewal tails list the same three cases).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. root hosting_ext_cloud_upgrade <- hosting_ext_overdue_renewal. Edge value_input, gate prorated_upgrade_share, form state, affirmative 'only after'. Four-point test: ordering connective; XX = term_end_date vs today (record words); no tool, id or code token; hard requirement on exactly that date. Unique resolver: only a holder-paid overdue renewal advances term_end_date past today for a plan whose term has ended (the early rule's scope excludes such a plan, the refund moves dates back, the upgrade never changes term dates, auto-renew attempts are over). Unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.hosting_holdings.489e7128-e28a-473e-bbf6-6ffaa9845754.term_end_date = 2026-10-15. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the renewal prices the upgrade at 0.00 on the ended term instead of the handling-time value. user_scenario never mentions the renewal, the lapse, declines, fees or the change request.

FACTOR CARD - hosting_ext_overdue_renewal (baseline = regular price for the new term length, which already follows the scheduled 24-month request; withdrawn 36-month request never counts): ovr_reseller_pct (parameter, account: Bronze 10); ovr_domain_bundle (method, domain: Harborline credits the bundled domain's yearly renewal against the hosting renewal - a bundled registration whose latest renewal line carries no refund and no later restore -> that line's amount per year renewed (17.64, as the domain charter billed it with the Bronze renewal discount), any other active bundled registration (free first year, refunded latest renewal, restored after it) -> its TLD's renewal_price, none -> no credit; cancelled/deleted registrations never count); ovr_mail_bundle (parameter, email: active Mail Plus, 6 seats -> 20.00); ovr_cert_bundle (parameter, ssl: an active OV certificate on the plan -> 12.00; OV/EV wins over DV when several are installed); ovr_late_fee (method, multi-source date + declines: per-day fee x days late after a fully declined cycle / percent of the regular price without one / none within 2 days; 3 days x 3.50 here). Credits never take more than half the discounted price (no zero or negative amount).
FACTOR CARD - hosting_ext_cloud_upgrade (no account tier discount: the account charter never applies one to proration lines; base hosting sentence superseded by a declared overwrite): upg_mail_bundle (parameter, email: active Mail Plus, 6 seats -> 20.00); upg_proration_unit (method: 24/36-month term with a whole month left -> whole months / term months; 1-month -> whole difference; otherwise days ratio); upg_outgrown_credit (parameter, history: only warnings (2026-09-29, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-11) are less than one calendar month old; the 2026-09-18 over_limit notice is the near-miss -> 20.00 fixed credit, not a percentage, so nothing compounds with the tier discount); upg_welcome_credit (parameter, history: no upgrade_proration line on the plan at all -> first-upgrade credit; lines only in earlier terms -> returning credit; a line in the current term -> none). The credits together never take more than half the prorated charge.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Renewal write: hosting_renewal.renewable_plan (status active, day 3 of 5 grace days); hosting_downgrade_and_term_change.downgrade_fits (no downgrade request; usage 140 sites / 171.4 GB). Upgrade write: hosting_upgrade_proration.upgrade_active (active); Cloud 8 is Cloud 4's only upgrade_target. No time gate. Overwrites: hosting_renewal pricing sentence (scoped, sibling of the early rule, identical case lists) and hosting_upgrade_proration charge sentence (scoped to Cloud 4 -> Cloud 8).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One plan 489e7128-e28a-473e-bbf6-6ffaa9845754; the renewal line pays the term starting 2026-10-15; the upgrade's amount paid = the checkout renewal line with that period_start (a refunded line is always an auto_renew line) + upgrade lines ending 2028-10-15 (none).

SEED. Cross rows priced by their own charters on their own dates: domain 0.00 (bundle_credit) 2024-10-15, 18.18 (2025-09-15, Business 0 percent), 17.64 (2026-09-15, Bronze 3 percent, from credit, matching ledger apply -17.64); deposit 500.00 on 2026-03-02 qualifies Bronze; balance 482.36 < the 24-month renewal so the auto-renew went to the card and declined; Mail Plus 6 seats 287.28 per year (Business 0 percent on both charge dates); OV Single Domain 62.99 on 2026-07-20 (69.99 less Bronze ssl 10 percent, card), certificate 2026-07-20 -> 2027-02-05 (200 days). Hosting: initial 299.88, auto-renew 599.88. Uptime reports were removed in round 2 (no rule reads them).

PERSONA. Brisk agency owner; volunteers the upgrade goal and that she pays by PayPal; identity on request; agrees to pay what is owed first when told; the expired card and the two-year term only when asked; completes both checkouts herself; ends after the upgrade receipt.

STANDARD SOLUTION. locate/verify -> read plan, charges, events, change requests, account, bundled domain and its charges, email and its charges, ledger, certificates and their charges -> hand over the overdue renewal (24 months, PayPal, request 301f35d2-3971-4499-83ed-469e8c9f6a3a) -> hand over the Cloud 8 upgrade (PayPal). Verification: /tmp/hosting_plans_and_billing_0076/t0/plan.py, every factor MOVES.
user_scenario: You are Corinne Halvorsen, the owner of Halvorsen Field Media LLC, a small web agency in Austin that hosts its clients' sites on one Harborline cloud plan set up for halvorsenfield.com. You are calling between client meetings, brisk and practical, and you speak in plain business terms rather than hosting jargon. Your goal: the sites have been crowding the Cloud 4 plan, so you want that plan moved up to Cloud 8 today. You will pay for the upgrade yourself through PayPal at Harborline's checkout once the support person sets it up for you, because you do not want anything charged to a card; you are not asking for anything else. Open with roughly: "Hi, this is Corinne from Halvorsen Field Media. Our Cloud 4 plan for halvorsenfield.com is running out of room and I'd like to move it up to Cloud 8 today - I'll pay for it myself through PayPal." You only give identity details when asked: your contact email is corinne@halvorsenfield.com and your phone is 7375550142; if a third detail is wanted, your support PIN is 248613. You do not know internal reference numbers and say so if asked. If the agent tells you something on the plan has to be paid or put right before the upgrade can be priced, you listen and say you will pay that too. If they ask how you will pay it, you say through PayPal at the checkout as well, because the card ending 2731 on file expired last month and you have not replaced it yet. If they ask how long the plan should run for, you say you set up a two-year term on the account in September and that is what you want. Whenever the agent hands a payment over for you to complete, you complete it yourself at the checkout with exactly the plan, the amount, the term and any request reference the agent gives you, choosing PayPal; you never invent an amount of your own. If a figure the agent quotes seems surprising you simply ask them to double-check it against the account, and accept their confirmation. Once the upgrade has gone through and you can see its receipt, you thank them briefly and end the call.

edges.condition: hosting_holdings.term_end_date of the plan is later than the date of today, which holds once the renewal line for the term starting on the previous term end date is billed and the term dates have advanced.
edges.policy_source: An upgrade charge is fixed only after the plan's term end date is later than today.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The plan's paid term ended on 2026-10-15 and today is 2026-10-18; all three auto-renew attempts of the cycle declined, so no renewal line pays a term starting 2026-10-15 and the term end date is not later than today.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's overdue renewal payment creates a renewal line with period_start 2026-10-15 and sets term_start_date 2026-10-15, term_end_date 2028-10-15, billing_term_months 24; the term end date is then later than today and the prorated upgrade share becomes 23/24 instead of a negative remainder (prorated charge 0).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the upgrade charge 'is fixed only after the plan's term end date is later than today', which only the overdue renewal brings about; in the reverse order the upgrade is priced on the ended term (remaining share negative, prorated charge 0, so the credits take nothing and the amount is 0.00) and the renewal is then priced on the Cloud 8 tier.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the overdue renewal and replaying the upgrade on the opening world gives 0.00 (prorated charge 0 on the ended term) instead of 880.99, and the terminal state lacks the renewal line and keeps term_end_date 2026-10-15.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to move the Cloud 4 plan up to Cloud 8 and says the customer pays by PayPal; it never mentions the ended term, the declined auto-renew attempts, a renewal, a late fee or the scheduled term change; it only reacts after the agent says something must be paid first ('If the agent tells you something on the plan has to be paid or put right before the upgrade can be priced ...') and answers the payment-method and term-length questions only when asked.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: buy_hosting_upgrade_8645a072 never reads the term dates or any renewal line: it checks only the payment-method literal, a positive amount, an official tier name and the plan's existence, then writes the upgrade line and the tier change; called on the opening world it writes faithfully and returns 'upgraded'. bill_overdue_hosting_renewal_c53aa4e7 checks no plan status, term date or eligibility (only the format contracts and that a named request is this plan's scheduled term change).
